Recognises food on photos and gives advice. Runs entirely on the phone. The model is about 2.6 GB and is only needed for photos and AI advice; everything else works without it.

Tarilka is a free, open-source, offline food and weight tracker. Data stays on your phone. Food values: USDA FoodData Central (public domain), typical Ukrainian labels and recipe calculations; the source is shown for each food. This app is not medical advice; for health conditions, pregnancy or eating disorders please talk to a doctor.
Water, tea, coffee and other drinks. Juice, kefir and other drinks logged as food are counted automatically.

Health Connect is not available on this phone. Steps will come from the phone\'s sensor.
Material You: accent colours follow your wallpaper.
Everything is stored only on this phone. Make a backup from time to time, or before switching phones.

In the file: %1$d food entries, %2$d drinks, %3$d weigh-ins, %4$d own foods. Everything current will be replaced: diary, sleep, cycle, bowel, workouts, waist, notes, own foods and favourites, and the profile if the backup has one.

1. Tap Download model: your browser downloads %1$s (about 2.6 GB, Wi-Fi recommended). It is Google\'s Gemma 4 E2B; it runs on most phones with 6 GB of memory or more.\n2. Come back and tap Choose model file. The app has no internet access, so this is the only way in.

The file is encrypted with the password (AES-256) and can be restored only with it. A forgotten password cannot be recovered. Several random words are the strongest and easiest to remember.
This backup is encrypted. Enter its password.
How do you feel today? Hunger, mood, sleep…

phone sensor, since first opened today

Foods you searched for, or the AI saw in a photo, that are not in the database (times in brackets). Kept only on this phone. You can add any of them yourself: Foods → New food. To get them into the database for everyone, tap Send the list: the list is passed to GitHub as the page opens and stays in the browser history; you can edit it there, and it is published from your account only when you confirm.

All food, fluid, weight, waist, sleep, cycle, bowel, workout, note and Why I eat records will be deleted. Your foods, recipes, profile and the AI model stay. This cannot be undone.

The diary (food, fluids, weight, waist, sleep, cycle, bowel, workouts, notes, Why I eat), your foods and recipes, favourites, profile, the photo portion correction, the phone-sensor step log and the Not found list will be deleted. Steps and sleep in Health Connect are not touched. The AI model and settings (language, theme, reminders) stay. This cannot be undone.
Also delete the records Tarilka wrote to Health Connect
Summaries for the week, month, year
Not enough entries yet: at least 3 days are needed.
Average vegetables and fruit a day (potatoes and dried fruit not counted). The WHO recommends at least 400 g.

Calories from sweets, pastries and sugary drinks (juice included), with the fat and flour in them. The WHO advises that free sugars (added sugar, honey, syrups, juice) give under 10% of calories, ideally under 5%; the sugar itself is less than these calories, so this is a rough guide.
Share of calories eaten after 22:00, by the time of the meal; you can set or correct it by tapping an entry.
A standard drink has 10 g of alcohol: about 250 ml of beer, 100 ml of wine or 30 ml of spirits. There is no safe amount of alcohol (WHO), so less is better.
Days with fast food: pizza, burgers, shawarma and so on. Now and then is fine.
A Sleep row on Today: hours slept in two taps. Used in summaries.
A Sleep row on Today: hours slept in two taps. If a watch or another app writes sleep to Health Connect, Tarilka reads it (with your permission). Used in summaries.
After adding food, a short question: hunger, stress, boredom, company or habit, how hungry you were and whether it was hard to stop. You can skip it. Helps to see patterns.
Hunger before eating: 1 none, 5 very strong

Average sleep. Adults are advised 7–9 hours; under 18, 8–10. With less sleep, appetite and sweet cravings go up. If you regularly sleep over 10 hours and still feel tired in the day, that is worth discussing with a doctor too.
How often you ate for a reason other than hunger (of the times you answered Why I eat). Eating for company or pleasure now and then is normal.
Noticed: more than 7 drinks a week.
Noticed: alcohol on 4 or more days a week.
Noticed days with 6 or more drinks: %1$d. That much at once is especially harmful.
If heavy days keep coming back or cutting down alone does not work, help from a doctor, a psychologist or a support line is a normal and effective step.
The first three questions of the WHO AUDIT test, about alcohol over the past year. A drink is 10 g of alcohol: 250 ml of beer, 100 ml of wine or 30 ml of spirits. Answers are not saved anywhere.
How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?
How many drinks do you have on a typical day when you drink?
How often do you have 6 or more drinks on one occasion?
Lower risk. Still, there is no safe amount, so less is better.
Increased risk. Try the tips below and set yourself a goal for the coming weeks: the app shows how the amount changes.
High risk to health. Start with the tips below. Help from a doctor, a psychologist or a support line is a normal and effective step, and the earlier the easier.
No data yet. Health Connect shows past days too; the phone sensor only days you opened the app.
On average %1$s a day · goal reached on %2$d of %3$d days

8,000 by default. Large studies show the health benefit grows up to about 6–8 thousand steps for people over 60 and 8–10 thousand for younger people, and then hardly increases. 10,000 comes from a 1960s pedometer advert.
Your own foods and recipes will be here. Add them with New food.
Favourite foods will be here. Tap the heart on what you eat often.
Trend: more than in the period before (it was %1$s).
Trend: less than in the period before (it was %1$s).
Trend: about the same as in the period before (%1$s).
Days with 400 g or more: %1$d of %2$d.
Days with a quarter of calories or more after 22:00: %1$d of %2$d.
If this goes on for weeks or it is hard to stop, talk to a doctor or a psychologist: it is common, and help (such as cognitive behavioural therapy) really works.
If poor sleep lasts several weeks and affects your days, see a doctor: insomnia is very treatable, including without medication.

All off; switch on only what you need. They come only when useful: if a meal is already logged, there is no reminder. Cycle reminders do not show on a screen locked with a PIN, password or fingerprint; the others show only Reminder there if the phone hides notification content. Tarilka asks for them not to be sent to a watch, but some watch and band apps ignore that.
%1$s of %2$s L so far. Time for a glass of water.
Time to wind down for sleep: dim the lights, put the phone away.
Your weekly summary is ready: Today → calendar at the top → Summaries.
At 12, 16 and 19 o\'clock, only if you drank clearly less than expected by then.
Notifications are not allowed. You can allow them in phone settings: Apps → Tarilka → Notifications.

Version: %1$s

What happened or what you would like:

The app\'s GitHub page opens (an account is needed). The feedback text is passed to it as the page opens and stays in the browser history; it is published only when you confirm, and shows your account name. Nothing from your diary is added.

Version: %1$s

Foods that were not found (times in brackets):
%2$s
A row on Today: how many times and what it was like, in two taps. Helps to see the link with fibre, fluids and movement.
A row on Today: what, how many minutes and how hard. The badge compares with the WHO recommendations.
Calories are a rough estimate for information; they are not added to the day\'s food target, as fitness estimates usually run high.

Workout minutes a week: moderate count as they are, vigorous double, light not counted. The WHO recommends adults 150–300 minutes of moderate activity a week and strength exercise on at least 2 days; under 18, at least 60 minutes of movement every day.
Days with a bowel movement out of the recorded ones. Anything from 3 times a week to 3 times a day is considered normal; being regular and effortless matters more.
Hard: %1$d days, loose: %2$d days. Fibre on average %3$s g a day.
See a doctor if there is blood or black stool, strong pain, unexplained weight loss, or changes lasting more than 2–3 weeks. Loose stools with fever or signs of dehydration are a reason too.
From your steps and workouts in recent weeks, your activity is closer to "%1$s" than the profile says. Update? Your daily target depends on it.

A row on Today: cycle day and the approximate next start. Started is one tap; flow and pain are optional. Explains weight and appetite changes. If another app writes your cycle to Health Connect, Tarilka can read it (with your permission).
Expected to start ~%1$s. Has your period started? You can mark a past date too
A better estimate and the ovulation estimate appear after two marked starts. Until then the date uses the usual length you gave.
Cycle lengths differ noticeably, so ovulation is not shown: a calendar estimate is unreliable here.
Dates are approximate. This is not contraception and not a way to plan a pregnancy precisely.
Mark a start on another date
Mark an end on another date

In the days before a period, appetite and sweet cravings often rise and weight can be 0.5–2 kg higher from water; that is normal. What helps: regular meals and complex carbs, less salt, coffee and alcohol, movement and sleep.

See a doctor if cycles are shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days, there has been no period for 3 months, a period lasts over 7 days or is very painful or heavy, you bleed between periods or after sex, or something changes sharply. If you could be pregnant, take a test.
Worth seeing a gynaecologist: %1$s There is often a simple explanation and good treatment.
heavy periods or strong pain two cycles in a row.
Before and in the first days of a period, weight is often 0.5–2 kg higher for a while from water.
Cycle: remind before the expected start
2 days after the expected date, if no start was marked.
Your cycle may start in the coming days (in %1$d d).
Has your cycle started? Mark it in Tarilka, a past date is fine.
The backup will include cycle data. A password is recommended.
When adding food you can set and correct the time of the meal. The late-eating badge and the AI\'s advice on meal rhythm use it. When off, time is neither shown nor used.
To compare, weigh yourself at the same time each day, ideally in the morning before eating.
When did your last period start?
How many days does it usually last?
Only for the first estimate. After that the app counts from your Started marks.
Several at once works too: "sauerkraut 100 g, potatoes 40 g, cutlet". Or dictate with the keyboard microphone.
The AI reads the whole list again. The first time can take up to a minute.
The AI did not answer within a minute. Kept what was read without it: use Replace for what was not found.
The AI found nothing. Kept what was read without it.
BMI %1$s. Under 18 it is judged by age charts, so no category is shown.

BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². For example, 70 kg and 1.65 m: 70 ÷ (1.65 × 1.65) ≈ 25.7.

WHO categories for adults: under 18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 normal; 25–29.9 overweight; 30 or more obesity (class I 30–34.9, II 35–39.9, III 40+).

What BMI does not show: how much is muscle and how much is fat, and where the fat is. Athletes with a lot of muscle can be "overweight" without extra fat; older people can be "normal" while losing muscle. For people of Asian origin the WHO suggests lower risk thresholds. Waist size (over 80 cm for women, over 94 cm for men) adds useful information.

BMI is a starting point for a conversation, not a judgement of you. If it is under 18.5 or your weight changes for no clear reason, talk to a doctor.

During pregnancy and breastfeeding the app does not offer weight loss or a calorie deficit. About 300 kcal are added to the target (EFSA: from +70 early in pregnancy to +500 late in pregnancy and while breastfeeding). In pregnancy weight gradually goes up, and that is normal. Your doctor can tell you how much to eat and how your weight should change.

Under 18 the app shows no calories and does not offer weight loss: the body is still growing, and counting calories at this age can do harm. Instead of calories you see protein, fibre, fluids and habits. If your weight worries you, including when it is high, see a paediatrician or family doctor: programmes for the whole family help most. What works at home: regular meals, more vegetables and fruit, water instead of sugary drinks, daily movement, enough sleep and less screen time.
BMI is under 18.5, so weight loss is not offered. If your weight is dropping on its own, or thoughts about food and weight get in the way of life, it is worth talking to a doctor.
Not below the safety floor: if you enter less, the app raises it to the floor.
Your own target is below the safety floor, so the app uses the floor.
Your weight is going down (%1$.1f kg a week) and your BMI is already under 18.5. Make sure you eat enough, and talk to a doctor about it.
If a doctor has limited your fluids (for example for the heart or kidneys), follow their amount.
There were more than 60 days between two of the recent starts. If you did not miss an entry, a gap that long is worth discussing with a doctor. If you did, mark the missed start on its past date.
The AI is still finishing the previous request. Try again in a minute.
Time: %1$s, as for the whole meal (change it in the meal\'s header).
Data deleted in Tarilka, but Health Connect did not allow deleting everything: check Tarilka\'s permissions in Health Connect.
No workouts logged in the last 7 days. Even 10 minutes of brisk walking counts: a good start.

Green is going well, amber is so-so, orange is worth attention. There is no red: these are hints, not grades.

The colour comes from the number on the badge, following WHO and other medical guidance. Better or worse compares with the previous period of the same length.

Badges appear once there are at least 3 days of entries. Tap a badge for what it means and what helps.
Not enough data yet to compare with the previous period.
about the same as the previous period (%1$s)
Each bar is the daily average for its stretch; the dashed line is the target. Tap a line for what it means and what helps.
Average over days with entries. Green is within 10% of the target, amber within 25%. One day decides little; the average matters.
Protein helps keep muscle and stay full, especially when losing weight. Good sources: cottage cheese, eggs, poultry, fish, beans.
Fibre helps digestion and fullness: vegetables, fruit, whole grains, beans. The target is at least 25 g a day (EFSA, WHO); with more food the app uses 14 g per 1000 kcal (US guidelines).

Average over days with entries: water and drinks you added, drinks logged as food (juice, kefir, milk) and soups (80 % of their weight); alcohol is not counted. The guide is at least the EFSA level (1.6 L for women and 2 L for men from drinks and soups); a bigger body that uses more energy needs a little more. More in heat, with activity, in pregnancy and while breastfeeding. The best daily sign is thirst and pale urine.
Weight change along the trend line, kg a week. Weight swings with water and the cycle, so the trend over several weeks matters, not single days. More than 1% of body weight a week is too fast.
Encrypt the diary and open with fingerprint or PIN

The diary (food, fluids, weight, sleep, cycle, notes), the profile (including pregnancy) and the Not found list are encrypted with a key kept in the phone\'s secure hardware. Tarilka opens with your fingerprint or the phone PIN, so anyone who knows the phone PIN can open Tarilka too. It locks when the screen turns off or after a minute in the background (up to 10 minutes while a file picker or the camera opened by Tarilka is on top). Export and deleting data ask for the fingerprint or PIN again. Not encrypted: settings, the step log, a few of today\'s numbers for reminders, and the expected cycle date if cycle reminders are on. Entries in Health Connect are not covered.

⚠ Important: if you ever remove the phone's screen lock completely (PIN and fingerprint), Android destroys the key and the diary can no longer be opened, only restored from a backup. Adding a new fingerprint does not reset the key.

So first make an encrypted backup: Options → Data → Export backup.

Entries in Health Connect are not covered by this protection.
The diary will be decrypted and Tarilka will open without fingerprint or PIN.
First set a screen lock on the phone (PIN, password or fingerprint).

The diary\'s key is gone: this happens when the phone\'s screen lock is removed. The entries can no longer be opened. You can start with an empty diary and restore a backup: Options → Data.
The encrypted entries will be deleted for good. You can then restore a backup. Continue?

Do not remove the phone\'s screen lock (PIN and fingerprint) while protection is on: Android destroys the key and the diary can no longer be opened. Turn protection off here first. Make encrypted backups regularly.
Add the profile (sex, age, height, weight, targets)

The report is made on the phone. The PDF is not encrypted: once saved or sent it is an ordinary file. For more than 31 days it shows one line per day instead of the full menu; bowel, workouts and Why I eat then appear only in the summary.
%1$s, %2$d y, %3$d cm, %4$s kg · targets: %5$s kcal, protein %6$s g, fluids %7$s L
For more than 31 days: one line per day and notes as a list; bowel, workouts and Why I eat appear only in the summary. The full menu is in reports of up to 31 days.
Made with Tarilka. Nutrition values are estimates from USDA data, labels and recipes; ✦ marks a portion estimated by AI from a photo. This is not a medical opinion.
Tarilka cannot be captured by screenshots or screen recording, and shows as a blank window in recent apps and screen sharing. Works separately from app protection.
Calories, daily average per stretch (dashed: target)
EFSA guide: fat 20–35 %, carbohydrates 45–60 % of calories; protein at least 0.83 g per kg of body weight.
Protein %1$s of %2$s g · fibre %3$s of %4$s g

Log food by search, as a typed list (\u201cbuckwheat 200 g, cutlet\u201d) or with a photo of your plate. Tarilka counts calories, protein, fibre and fluids and shows habits as coloured badges, without judgement.

The app has no internet permission, no accounts and no ads. Tarilka itself sends nothing; if you turn on Health Connect, apps you allow there can see those records. If you like, the diary can be encrypted and opened with your fingerprint (Options → App protection), and a backup saved with a password (Options → Data).

Sleep, cycle, workouts, bowel, Why I eat, reminders and on-device AI can be turned on in Options whenever you want. Start with the profile: height, weight and goal, and Tarilka works out your targets. One question to finish: are you 18 or older? Under 18 Tarilka shows no calories.
Tarilka closed with an error last time

You can send a technical description of the error to help fix it. It holds only the error\'s name, places in the code and the Tarilka and Android versions, no diary entries. The text is passed to a public GitHub page as it opens and stays in the browser history; you can edit it there, and it is published only when you confirm.

Measure with a tape halfway between the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone (often at the navel), breathing out, every 2–4 weeks. By WHO, the risk for the heart and metabolism is higher over %1$s cm and substantially higher over %2$s cm. The waist shows what BMI cannot: where fat is stored.
The waist adds to BMI: it shows where fat is stored. Measuring every 2–4 weeks is enough.
Options: swap some mayonnaise for yoghurt or 15% sour cream, sausage for baked chicken, fried for baked. Nuts, oil and fish are healthy fats; only the portion matters there.
Sausages, frankfurters, ham: %1$s days a week (%2$s). Try chicken, fish, eggs or beans on 2 of those days: processed meat raises the risk of bowel cancer.
Red meat: about %1$s g a week (%2$s). Up to 350–500 g cooked is advised; some days can be fish, poultry or beans.

Sweets and sugary drinks give %1$s%% of calories (%2$s). The WHO advises that free sugars (added sugar, honey, syrups, juice) give under 10%%, ideally 5%%; sugar is only part of these calories, so this is a rough guide. A step for the week: half the sugar in tea, fruit instead of one dessert, water instead of a sweet drink.

Foods rich in saturated fat give %1$s%% of calories (%2$s). The WHO advises saturated fat under 10%% of calories. Options: oil instead of butter or lard, yoghurt or 10–15%% sour cream instead of cream and full-fat sour cream, bake instead of fry.
Fast food: %1$s days a week (%2$s). A home-made version of the same usually has less salt and fat.
Only %1$s%% of bread and grains is whole grain (mostly %2$s). On some days try buckwheat, oats or whole-grain bread.
Vegetables and fruit: %1$s g a day of 400. Add one more portion to what you usually have.
Hardly any beans or lentils. Beans, lentils, chickpeas or peas at least 2–3 times a week give protein and fibre.
Hardly any fish. Twice a week is advised, once oily: herring, mackerel, salmon.
A handful of nuts or seeds (25–30 g) several times a week gives healthy fats, if there is no allergy.
Vegetables and fruit: %1$s g a day, over 400 g.
Beans or lentils: %1$s times a week.
Fish: %1$s times a week, oily included.
%1$s%% of bread and grains is whole grain (%2$s).
In pregnancy, while breastfeeding and under 18 we do not rate waist size: the adult thresholds do not apply, and the body is changing, which is normal.
BMI %1$s. In pregnancy and while breastfeeding we do not rate BMI: the body is changing, and that is normal.
In pregnancy, while breastfeeding and under 18, the safest choice is no alcohol at all. If stopping is hard, tell your doctor: it is common, and help is available.

If everything is logged, this week you ate clearly less on average than your body uses even at rest. Long-term undereating takes energy, muscle and sleep, and often leads to overeating. If this comes from worries about weight or food, talk to a doctor or a psychologist: help works.
Protein %1$s g · fibre %2$s g a day. Under 18 we do not show a calorie target: needs differ a lot while the body is growing. Go by hunger and fullness, regular meals and a variety of foods.

Very little food is logged today. If that is real, it is too little for a growing body: regular meals are needed. Check whether something is missing.

resources.string: cycle length outside 21–45 days (the usual range under 18).
Health Connect does not allow Tarilka to write. Permissions can be changed in Health Connect → Apps → Tarilka.
Only some permissions were given: only what you allowed (food, drinks or weight) will be written.

Tarilka has no internet access and sends data nowhere. From Health Connect it only reads steps, sleep and the menstrual cycle (if you allowed it) to show them in the diary, and writes food, drinks and weight when "Write to Health Connect" is on. Records in Health Connect are visible to apps you allow there. Any permission can be taken back in Health Connect → Apps → Tarilka.
